drawdown_context: -66.0% from 52w high, +14% above 52w low. Filing is the FY25 10-K (fiscal year ended Aug 30, 2025); two subsequent 10-Qs were filed within the cutoff window — Q1 FY26 (filed 2026-01-08, period ending Nov 29, 2025) and Q2 FY26 (filed 2026-04-09, period ending Feb 28, 2026). rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'During the fifty-two weeks ended August 30, 2025, our net sales increased $119.6 million, or 9.0%, to $1,450.9 million ... driven by Quest and OWYN volume growth, which more than offset continued declines in Atkins driven primarily by a reduction of distribution.' Disaggregated NA brand sales: Atkins $420.8M FY25 vs $492.0M FY24 (-14.5%) vs $526.8M FY23; Quest $863.6M (+11.1% YoY); OWYN $137.0M (vs $29.2M partial-period FY24). 10-K risk factor adds: 'During fiscal year 2025, Walmart reduced the number of Atkins products it carries in its stores and in the future may continue to reduce the total assortment of Atkins products it carries.' Implied claim: Atkins decline is contained / mature; Quest + OWYN are the growth engines and the portfolio is healthy.
rfm_tuples.f: If the 'Quest + OWYN offsets Atkins decline' framing is durable, subsequent 10-Qs should show Quest and OWYN continuing to grow and Atkins decline rate stabilizing — NOT accelerating across the portfolio.

Q2 FY26 (13 wks to Feb 28 2026): total net sales $326.0M vs $359.7M (-9.4% YoY) — Quest $211.4M nearly flat (+0.3%), Atkins $79.7M vs $108.7M (-26.7%), OWYN $28.1M vs $33.8M (-16.8%). Six-month FY26 total $666.2M vs $700.9M FY25H1 (-5.0%). claim_evolution on 'reduction of distribution' phrase: SILENT_POST_CLAIM (0 mentions in subsequent filings) — the 10-K's framing language disappears even as the underlying problem accelerates.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K's '+9.0% revenue growth, Quest/OWYN offset Atkins' framing decisively breaks in the very next two quarters. By Q2 FY26: (a) Quest growth has flatlined (the offset engine), (b) OWYN has reversed from growth to -17% decline (acquisition thesis failing), and (c) Atkins decline ACCELERATED from -14.5% FY annual to -26.7% in Q2. The composite is no longer 'one weak brand inside two growing brands' — it is now 'all three brands declining or flat' with $34M YoY sales loss in a single quarter. The 'reduction of distribution' framing language vanishes from subsequent disclosure (SILENT_POST_CLAIM) even though the problem manifestly worsened — this is the canonical disclosed-but-rapidly-stale claim pattern.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 5 Goodwill & Intangibles + MD&A: 'Loss on impairment charges were $60.9 million for the fifty-two weeks ended August 30, 2025' attributed to the Atkins brand indefinite-lived intangible and the licensing-agreements finite-lived intangible. Critical Audit Matter from Deloitte specifically calls out 'The Company's evaluation of the Atkins indefinite-lived intangible asset for impairment involves the comparison of its estimated fair value to its carrying amount.' Filing also states OWYN goodwill was tested and 'fair value was greater than its carrying value, resulting in no impairment charges related to goodwill.' Implied claim: the impairment is sized to actual deterioration, and OWYN intangibles are safe.
rfm_tuples.f: If the FY25 impairment is properly sized to the underlying brand deterioration, subsequent 10-Qs should not record additional material impairment charges within 6-9 months. A material follow-on impairment would indicate the FY25 charge was undersized / management was slow-walking write-downs.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q2 FY26 10-Q Note: 'As a result of the declines of net sales and future revenue projections assessed during the second quarter of fiscal year 2026, the Company identified a triggering event ... resulting in a loss on impairment of $187.0 million for OWYN and $62.0 million for Atkins during the thirteen weeks ended February 28, 2026.' Total Q2 FY26 impairment = $249.0 million. Cumulative impairment since Q4 FY25 = $60.9M + $249.0M = $309.9M in 2 quarters. Q2 FY26 income from operations = -$213.3M (vs +$54.7M prior year). Q2 FY26 net loss = -$159.7M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The FY25 10-K impairment of $60.9M was materially undersized. Within 6 months the company took a $249M follow-on charge ($187M against OWYN — the acquisition closed June 2024 for $281.9M, meaning ~66% of the acquisition price has been written off in 21 months — plus another $62M against Atkins on top of the FY25 Atkins charge). The 10-K's explicit statement that OWYN goodwill was tested in Q4 FY25 and 'fair value was greater than carrying value' is technically true at the test date but the OWYN business deteriorated so fast that a triggering event fired one quarter later. Critical Audit Matter on Atkins was correctly flagged by Deloitte — the auditor identified the risk; management still under-sized the FY25 charge. This is the hard signal that the 10-K narrative was OBSCURING the magnitude of intangible deterioration.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 1 Business and Item 1A Risk Factors: 'A substantial majority of our sales are generated from a limited number of retailers. Sales to our largest retailer, Walmart Inc., represented approximately 31% of consolidated sales in fiscal year 2025, with approximately 24% through their mass retail channel and approximately 7% through their Sam's Club and e-commerce channels.' Note 15: Customer 1 = 31% / 31% / 31% across FY25/FY24/FY23. Customer 2 = 18% / 18% / 16%. So top-2 customers = 49% of total sales; both well above SEC 10% disclosure threshold. Walmart is also actively reducing Atkins SKU count.
rfm_tuples.f: If retailer-concentration risk were just disclosure boilerplate, megacap 10-K/10-Q/8-K filings on Walmart and Amazon should not be expected to name Simply Good Foods (consumer-staples primes rarely name individual CPG vendors). The risk is not megacap-side disclosure absence (a known false-positive for restaurant/CPG verticals) — it is the EXPOSURE itself when paired with the disclosed Walmart-driven Atkins SKU cuts.
rfm_tuples.M_source: revenue_concentration (via filing cross-read) + megacap_namecheck.query_megacap_mentions (Walmart, Amazon) + 10-K risk-factor parse
rfm_tuples.M_value: Customer concentration (filing cross-read): top customer = 31%, top-2 = 49%. SEC threshold is 10% — both customers materially above. Walmart explicitly disclosed as Atkins-distribution-reducer in fiscal 2025. megacap_namecheck: 0 hits for 'Simply Good Foods' in Walmart or Amazon 10-K/10-Q/8-K over 10-year window → INFLATION_SUSPECT signal, but this is the known consumer-staples false positive (megacaps don't name individual CPG vendors at sub-10% of their own revenue).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K honestly discloses both the 31%/18% concentration AND that Walmart is actively reducing Atkins SKUs. The lying-detector framework's job here is to recognize that the disclosed concentration is genuinely informative when paired with the disclosed Walmart SKU cuts AND the Q2 FY26 -27% Atkins decline. The combination is structurally riskier than the 10-K's MD&A tone conveys — at 31% concentration, a single retailer's category-management decision (cutting Atkins) cascades directly into the headline P&L. Megacap-side absence is not a lying signal here (the consumer-staples false positive applies). Severity is MODERATE because the disclosure is technically complete but the framing 'long-term Walmart relationship' obscures the ongoing SKU-reduction risk that Q2 FY26 results validated.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: '$98.5 million in cash as of August 30, 2025. We believe our sources of liquidity and capital will be sufficient to finance our continued operations.' 'approximately $250 million in outstanding term loan indebtedness and a revolving credit facility with availability of up to $75 million with no amounts drawn.' 'We were in compliance with all financial covenants as of August 30, 2025.' Term Facility effective rate 6.3%, maturity March 17, 2027. Revolver covenant: max total net leverage 6.00x ONLY if revolver drawn >30% of commitments — currently undrawn, so covenant is dormant.
rfm_tuples.f: If liquidity is genuinely strong, going-concern detector should be NEGATIVE, auditor should be clean, and no late-cycle covenant amendments under distress should be needed.

Operating cash flow FY25 was strong (the term loan was subsequently INCREASED $150M to $400M in early FY26 to extend maturity to March 2030 — see C5 — and that was an opportunistic refinancing, not a distress event). UCC proxy's ELEVATED_LIEN_EXPOSURE signal is mechanically driven by the multiple term-loan amendment exhibits routinely filed since 2017 — NOT a new distress signature. rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Liquidity discussion frames refinancing capacity as routine: 'The Company entered into the 2025 Repricing Amendment' (most recent listed amendment at filing date), with the credit agreement's history of repricings (2022, 2023, 2025) and the Sixth Amendment in June 2024 to fund OWYN. rfm_tuples.f: If the credit facility were genuinely healthy, post-filing capital actions (term-loan upsizings, repricings) should look like opportunistic liability management rather than distress refinancing, and should not coincide with collapsing brand economics.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Q2 FY26 10-Q Note 8: Term Facility balance = $400.0M (up from $250.0M at Aug 30 2025), via the '2026 Incremental Facility Amendment' which increased the principal by $150.0M AND extended maturity from March 17, 2027 to March 17, 2030. Effective rate at Feb 28 2026 = 5.7% (improved from 6.3% at Aug 30 2025 — the repricing actually got cheaper). Also extended revolving commitments. Q2 FY26 affirms 'in compliance with all covenants.' The $150M of incremental debt + $200M new share-repurchase authorization (Jan 6, 2026) suggests management chose to lever up at the trough to fund buybacks, not to plug a liquidity hole.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The credit-facility relationship IS healthy and bank-syndicate-friendly. The 2026 Incremental Facility Amendment got CHEAPER pricing (6.3% → 5.7%), extended maturity by 3 years, and provided $150M of additional dry powder — this is the opposite of distressed liability management (compare to FMC pilot's 8.45% subordinated notes at distressed coupon). The $200M buyback authorization announced Jan 2026 paired with the term-loan upsizing indicates management is using debt capacity to repurchase at trough valuations, NOT to fund operating losses. Banks are voluntarily participating at improved terms despite the brand impairment news — this validates the underlying cash-generation thesis even as the equity story deteriorates. PASS.

Q2 FY26 management commentary: 'one-time effects from actions taken to mitigate OWYN product quality issues' — this language appears NOWHERE in the FY25 10-K. rfm_tuples.interpretation: The OWYN narrative collapse is the single sharpest lying/obscuring signal in this filing pack. The FY25 10-K (filed Oct 28, 2025) treated OWYN as the integration success story (segment growth from $29M partial to $137M full year) and explicitly tested OWYN goodwill in Q4 FY25 with no impairment. Six months later: $187M impairment + first explicit public acknowledgement of 'OWYN product quality issues.' Product quality issues do not arise overnight — they were either (a) known internally during the 10-K period and not disclosed, or (b) the integration was being managed at a level that masked underlying operational deterioration. The 'we may not realize expected benefits' boilerplate risk factor was technically prophylactic but the MD&A narrative tone (segment aggregation language, no quality flags) actively obscured the speed of the underlying breakdown. This is the canonical 'fact disclosed-too-late' pattern.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Insider sales: 37 Form 4 filings over 365-day window, 10 sales totaling $485K, 1 proximate sale ($27K, transaction code F = tax withholding on vesting, NOT discretionary), 0 discretionary proximate sales, signal=ROUTINE_10B5_1. Buyback execution: Jan 6, 2026 the company RE-AUTHORIZED the repurchase program at $200M (resetting from the Oct 2025 $150M increase). As of Feb 28, 2026 ~$182.5M of the $200M January authorization remained — i.e., only ~$17.5M actually repurchased between Jan 6 and Feb 28, despite the trough valuation and the $150M of fresh term-loan capacity.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Insider behavior is clean (no discretionary cluster, tiny aggregate sales), so no information-asymmetry red flag from Form 4 activity. BUT the buyback velocity tells a different story: management raised the authorization to $200M in January 2026 (signaling 'we will buy the trough'), levered up $150M of cheap term-loan, and then executed only ~$17.5M of buybacks in the next ~8 weeks. This is the buyback-deceleration-at-trough pattern flagged in the SIGOS methodology (analogous to UPWK's slowdown) — management's TALK about buybacks at trough significantly exceeds their actions, suggesting lower internal conviction in the trough valuation than the public framing implies. Severity is MODERATE not SEVERE because the authorization is real and large; the gap between talk and walk is the signal.

summary: SMPL is a consumer-defensive name whose -66% drawdown is being driven by a structurally accelerating Atkins/OWYN brand deterioration that the 10-K narrative materially under-conveys. Three SEVERE claims all sit in the lying/obscuring zone: (C1) the 10-K '+9% growth, Atkins offset' framing collapses in the very next two 10-Qs (Q2 FY26 reveals Quest flat, OWYN -17%, Atkins -27%, total -9.4% YoY); (C2) the FY25 $60.9M impairment was materially undersized — $249M follow-on charge in Q2 FY26 brings 6-month impairment to $310M; (C6) OWYN was treated as integration success in the 10-K with no goodwill impairment in Q4 FY25, then -66% of $281.9M purchase price was written off 6 months later coinciding with first public acknowledgement of 'OWYN product quality issues.' Liquidity (C4) and credit facility (C5) are HONEST positives — Deloitte clean since 2019, NO_GOING_CONCERN, $400M term loan repriced down to 5.7% with maturity extended to 2030, $200M buyback authorization. Audit (C8) PASS — Deloitte's CAM on Atkins was correct, the auditor signaled risk and management still under-reserved. Customer concentration (C3) and buyback velocity (C7) are MODERATE — disclosed but framed more reassuringly than the post-trough reality. Composite 0.333 across 8 verifiable claims (3 PASS / 2 MOD / 3 SEV / 0 RED / 0 UNV) — sits ABOVE the 0.30 small-cap loose admission threshold, so SMPL is EXCLUDED from the long universe. This is the framework working: a name that is not fraudulent but is materially obscuring the speed of intangible deterioration in its core brands.
